name: LegionWareX
summary: A medieval high-fantasy adventure sandbox built around Bloom Level-Up: dragons, monsters, bosses, magic, knights, new biomes, decor, shaders and Fresh Animations, with Better Combat. Minecraft 1.20.1 (Forge).
_comment: FreshOrangeSlices' LegionWareX (2026-10-26), from the Medieval High Fantasy master list and goals docs: a sandbox full of optional content, no required ending, dangerous but not miserable, multiplayer first. Combat route: Better Combat (not Epic Fight); Better Mob Combat is shelved (its mob animation hook crashes the server on creatures from Mowzie's, Migamigos, Cataclysm, Legendary Monsters and Monster Expansion, and with the whole pack on vanilla wolves too; its last build is from January 2025). After the first playtest: Novum's Altitude out (its sky effects made the world disorienting), Ice and Fire out (its dragons wreck buildings, and its 1.20.1 build is a beta), Mowzie's Mobs out, and a bosses layer in their place. Magic: Iron's Spells, plus the RPG Series' Paladins & Priests and Rogues & Warriors (no Wizards, Elemental Wizards or Archers). No voice chat (friends should be able to join with nothing extra). Mods are in cumulative layers so CI can tell which layer breaks what; the shipped pack is every layer. Forge 47.4.28 (1.20.1's recommended; Iron's Spells and others need 47.4+). Modrinth projects by slug (newest 1.20.1 Forge release or beta; required dependencies are added automatically, and the few a mod needs without saying so on Modrinth, such as Iron's Lib, are listed next to it; Migamigos' Framework is CurseForge-only, so it's packed inside). Bloom and the CurseForge-only mods ('external') are packed inside, which is fine for sharing with friends but not for publishing.

layers.name: core
layers._comment: Bloom with Better Combat and the Fresh Animations set (the earlier Forge pack), plus the performance mods, since they change how everything renders: Embeddium, ModernFix, FerriteCore, Clumps, Entity Culling (doesn't draw what's out of sight), ImmediatelyFast (faster HUD and text drawing), AI Improvements (cheaper mob AI), Let Me Despawn (mobs that picked up items still despawn, dropping them), and for the server, Chunky (pre-generate the world) and spark (find what lags). Open Loader puts the pack's own data pack (pack_data) into every world and the server.

layers.name: creatures
layers._comment: Creatures, bosses and companions, and the spawn and structure control that keeps them memorable instead of everywhere. Zoni's Companions (FreshOrangeSlices' pick, beside Migamigos) are only summoned, from devices players craft, never found in the wild; its Ultimate Summon Device (catches any mob, bosses included) is taken out and its creative-only items are hidden (pack_data).

layers.name: magic-and-gear
layers._comment: Iron's Spells as the mage, the RPG Series' Paladins & Priests and Rogues & Warriors (Spell Engine comes with them), weapons and armor, and the recipe glue for all of it. Marium's Soulslike Weaponry is on test (power creep).

layers.name: animation-and-qol
layers._comment: The rest of the visual stack (Punchy! stays unless testing shows it fights Better Combat; Oculus, the Forge port of Iris, with Complementary Unbound picked, Solas to swap to, and MakeUp Ultra Fast for weaker PCs), and the quality-of-life and multiplayer mods. Keybind Atlas replaced KeyVision (FreshOrangeSlices' playtest: KeyVision took over the Controls screen and had no mouse buttons); it's a separate keyboard-and-mouse map on Ctrl+K, so the normal Controls list is back.

layers.name: bosses
layers._comment: Bosses in place of Ice and Fire and Mowzie's Mobs (first playtest): L_Ender's Cataclysm (dungeon bosses), Legendary Monsters (roaming early, middle and late game bosses), Bosses'Rise (Souls-like bosses), The Graveyard (graveyards, crypts and their undead) and Illager Invasion (new illagers to fight), Bosses Oddities (more unusual bosses; CurseForge-only, packed inside) and GTBC's Cataclysmic Boss UI (a screen before each Cataclysm boss fight with its lore, attacks and tips), the last two FreshOrangeSlices' picks. CI summons every one of their creatures with the rest of the pack.

layers.name: world-and-decor
layers._comment: Biomes O' Plenty for the world (FreshOrangeSlices' pick; Terralith's biomes felt too big), and Decorative Blocks and Handcrafted for building (beams, braziers, chains, lattices and seats; vanilla-style furniture). BOP's Nether is cut back (config_files): Visceral Heap and Withered Abyss are off, and its Nether regions weigh 5 against vanilla's 10 (BOP's default is 13, more than half the Nether). Every Compat (Wood Good) makes the decor in BOP's woods too (and in any other mod's woods it knows); its blocks have their own creative tab.

config_files._comment: For both sides (the server, and the worlds a player makes; Forge copies defaultconfigs into each new world). A safety net: an entity or block entity that errors while ticking is removed and logged instead of crashing the server. Legionary's Unbreakable boss shoots flaming skulls and magma blocks whose code needs a client-only class, so each one crashes a dedicated server on its first tick (found by the mob check); with this they fizzle instead.
config_files._biomesoplenty: BOP's own files with two Nether biomes off (Visceral Heap's flesh, Withered Abyss's void pits) and its Nether region weight 5 instead of 13 (vanilla's is 10), so about two thirds of the Nether stays vanilla. The Overworld is BOP's default.
config_files.config/biomesoplenty/generation.toml:
[nether]
	#The weighting of bop biome regions in the nether.
	bop_nether_region_weight = 5
	#The weighting of rare bop biome regions in the nether.
	bop_nether_rare_region_weight = 2

[overworld]
	#The weighting of primary bop biome regions in the overworld.
	bop_primary_overworld_region_weight = 10
	#The weighting of rare bop biome regions in the overworld.
	bop_overworld_rare_region_weight = 2
	#The weighting of secondary bop biome regions in the overworld.
	bop_secondary_overworld_region_weight = 8
config_files._mutantmonsters: Mutant Monsters' spawn weights, as a share of each vanilla counterpart's: 10% (default 5%; FreshOrangeSlices: twice as common). Forge fills in the rest of the file.

pins._comment: Mods held at a version, even with --update (the lock only holds the last tested): each with why, so it can go once a fixed version is out.

keybind-atlas.why: 2.1.0 (2026-10-28) isn't remapped for a real game (built with development names), so the client crashes while loading

pack_data._comment: LegionWareX's own data pack, loaded into every world (new and old) and the server by Open Loader, from config/openloader/data/legionwarex: the recipes the pack takes out (each replaced by one that never loads), the items it takes out of the game (removed_items: their recipes, loot table entries and JEI listing, found in the mods' own files when the pack is built), and the items it hides from JEI (the c:hidden_from_recipe_viewers tag). Grouped by reason. CI checks the recipes are gone and the hidden items carry the tag (pack-data, from Bloom's registry dump).
pack_data.name: legionwarex
pack_data.description: LegionWareX: recipes the pack takes out, items it hides from JEI

removed_items._comment: FreshOrangeSlices' armory trim (2026-10-28, from the LegionWareX Armory page: every weapon sorted into own skill, own effect, stat bonus or nothing of its own). 230 weapons out: their recipes never load, the loot tables that name them are rewritten without them, and they're hidden from JEI. Ones a mod drops from its own code (some boss drops) can only be hidden; the pack summary lists them. Kept on purpose: the six Epic Knights shortswords the bigger swords are made from, the Knight's Sword (makes the Knight Summoner), the Decrepit Flamberge (repaired into the Legionnaire Flamberge), Monster Expansion's wooden mace and spear (Hunter's Notes) and Rimescourge (a quest reward).

spawns._comment: FreshOrangeSlices' playtest (2 hours, almost no modded mobs): the pack's natural spawns, aimed at about 1 in 5 of the mobs that spawn at night in every overworld biome (Biomes O' Plenty's included) being modded, about 1 in 20 being a structure's regulars out in biomes that fit them, bosses only in their lairs, at the same mob cap (vanilla's). Counted by mobs, not weight: vanilla monsters come in fours, most modded ones alone. Skarrier Mobs listed 15 of its mobs in every biome of every dimension at high weights, though each only spawns in one biome, underground, or after the Wither is beaten, so about half of all spawn picks failed; those are put back only where they can spawn. Graveyard and Cataclysm pick their biomes by tags, which only named vanilla biomes; the tags now take BOP's in. Mutant Monsters' weights are in its config (config_files). The pack test reports each biome's modded share (pack-spawns).

quiet.why: Biomes the pack adds no monsters to: vanilla's own peaceful ones (the Deep Dark is the Warden's, Mushroom Fields have none) and Biomes O' Plenty's (Auroral Garden has none, Mystic Grove few).

monsterexpansion:skrythe_biomes.why: Skrythe (750 health) spawns from its lair when the lair generates (one per 60x60 chunks where the biome fits); the lair could go in almost any overworld biome. Mountains only (FreshOrangeSlices).

graveyard:ghoul_spawns.why: Emptied: ghouls come from the pack's own spawns below (all land but quiet biomes).

graveyard:revenant_spawns.why: Emptied: revenants come from the pack's own spawns below (every snowy biome, smaller packs).

graveyard:nightmare_spawns.why: Emptied: nightmares come from the pack's own spawns below (open, dry and high land).

cataclysm:koboleton_spawn.why: Emptied: koboletons come from the pack's own spawns below (every dry biome).

ghouls.why: The Graveyard's ghouls (packs of 2-5): vanilla forests, taigas and swamps at weight 25; now all land (BOP's too) at 40.

revenants.why: The Graveyard's revenants: three vanilla snowy biomes in packs of 5-8 (weight 25); now every snowy biome, 3-5 at weight 12.

nightmares.why: The Graveyard's nightmares (alone): open land as before, and BOP's dry and high land; weight 20 (was 10).

koboletons.why: Cataclysm's koboletons (its desert ruins' regulars, 2-3): vanilla deserts, savannas and badlands at 15; now every dry biome, and savannas, at 35.

skarrier_caves.why: Underground in the dark (not the Deep Dark); Bowlder and Gorger only after the Wither is beaten. One Bowlder and one Wrought within 100 blocks.

skarrier_frozen_peaks.why: Freeze: vanilla Ice Spikes, Frozen Peaks and Snowy Slopes, after the Wither.

skarrier_ice_spikes.why: Frost: vanilla Ice Spikes, under the open sky.

skarrier_swamps.why: Slithers: vanilla Swamp and Mangrove Swamp, above Y 60 (at 120 they took over swamps).

skarrier_swamp.why: Gadlisk: vanilla Swamp, after the Wither.

skarrier_badlands.why: Viruleon (one within 100 blocks, after the Wither): vanilla badlands and desert.

skarrier_end.why: Voidrake: End Barrens and End Highlands, after the Wither.

monster_expansion_animals.why: Arborix and Kobeko (neutral, spawn like animals, in daylight too) as before, and in BOP's land biomes.

jungle_wild.why: Zombiflore (Skarrier, no spawn condition of its own): every jungle, not just vanilla's.

desert_bombers.why: Bombers (Legendary Monsters, vanilla Desert at 75): BOP's deserts too, fewer.

forest_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Illager Invasion's fort crew, The Graveyard's corrupted illagers and Iron's Spells' catacombs zombies out of their forts, crypts and catacombs, in forests and taigas.

village_crew.why: About 1 in 20: The Graveyard's overrun-village crew, Illager Invasion's marauders and Iron's Spells' catacombs zombies on open land.

desert_crew.why: About 1 in 20: The Graveyard's desert-village crew in dry lands (Cataclysm's koboletons come by their tag above).

snow_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Cataclysm's draugr out of the Frosted Prison, in snowy biomes.

mountain_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Myths & Legends' possessed armor out of its old camps, in mountains.

swamp_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Illager Invasion's alchemists (they throw potions) in swamps.

jungle_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Legendary Monsters' mossy golems out of the Mossy Temple, in jungles.

conditional._comment: Mobs the pack test leaves out of a biome's modded share: they only spawn underground, after the Wither, or under a condition of their own.

client_presets._resource_packs: Bottom to top, above vanilla's Default (and Forge's mod resources). Bloom switches them on before the game first reads options.txt, once per change of this list (client/mixin/OptionsMixin).
client_presets._shader: Shaders on with Complementary Unbound at first launch (and once per change of this line); K turns shaders off, O picks another pack (Solas and the much lighter MakeUp Ultra Fast ship too).
client_presets._keys: Key bindings set once per change of this list (by name, as options.txt has them): Oculus's 'reload shaders' is unbound (it was R, and a stray press freezes the game for seconds while the shader rebuilds), and Keybind Atlas opens on Ctrl+K (it started on K, Oculus's shader toggle; Alt+K is its own 'cycle keybind sets').

files._comment: Client config files, as given (the mod fills in every setting left out). FreshOrangeSlices wants Minecraft's own title screen: Aquamirae swaps in its frozen-sea panorama and logo. Inventory Profiles Next's sort buttons sat on top of the Spell Binding Table's spell list (FreshOrangeSlices' playtest): an IPN hint switches IPN off on that screen (the table has nothing to sort).
